title: How much green paint is made?
description: Two thirds of a litre of yellow paint and three fourths of a litre of blue paint are mixed. The amounts are added with a common bottom number of twelve, and the sum is checked against one litre.
teaching_notes: One idea: mixing two amounts means adding them, so the fractional units are made the same first. Watch for students who add the bottom numbers.

video_script.why: A learner uses the solved method on a real problem: find a common bottom number, rewrite both fractions, add the top numbers, and write the sum as a whole and a fraction.
video_script.anchor: two paint tins, one holding two thirds of a litre of yellow paint and one holding three fourths of a litre of blue paint
video_script.payoff_line: one and five twelfths litres of green paint

final_answer.spoken: seventeen twelfths of a litre, which is one and five twelfths litres of green paint

video_script.fraction_reading: two thirds, three fourths, eight twelfths, nine twelfths, seventeen twelfths, five twelfths

names.{{NAME_7}}: person in the book problem who mixes yellow paint and blue paint to make green paint

never_show: the total volume before the step that adds the top numbers
maths_rules: 3 and 4 share no factor, so the common bottom number is 12
check: 2/3 > 1/2 and 3/4 > 1/2, so the sum is more than 1 litre
video_script.design: Two tins stay on the board with their amounts. Each amount is rewritten in twelfths, the top numbers are added, and the sum is split into one whole and five twelfths.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a tin of yellow paint marked 2/3 litre and a tin of blue paint marked 3/4 litre; a question mark over an empty tin

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears and a person stands beside two paint tins
marks.amounts: the tins are marked 2/3 litre and 3/4 litre
marks.ask: a question mark appears over an empty tin

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. {{NAME_7}} mixes yellow paint and blue paint.
<bookmark mark='amounts'/>The yellow paint is two thirds of a litre. The blue paint is three fourths of a litre.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much green paint is made?

beats.on_screen: the tins hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the two paints pour into the empty tin; the note mixing is adding appears; the fractions 2/3 and 3/4 sit side by side with a question mark

marks.mix: the two paints pour into the empty tin and the note mixing is adding appears
marks.unit: thirds and fourths sit side by side with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='mix'/>Mixing two paints means adding their amounts.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Thirds and fourths are different fractional units, so we make them the same first.

beats.on_screen: Given: yellow paint 2/3 litre; blue paint 3/4 litre
narration: <bookmark mark='yellow'/>Given, the yellow paint is two thirds of a litre.
<bookmark mark='blue'/>The blue paint is three fourths of a litre.

beats.on_screen: To find: the volume of green paint
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the volume of green paint.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: green paint = 2/3 + 3/4; 3 and 4 share no factor, so use 12

marks.twelve: 3 x 4 = 12 is written and 12 is circled

beats.colours: the common bottom number 12 = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, mixing means adding, so we add two thirds and three fourths.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Three and four share no factor, so the common bottom number is twelve.

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, two thirds is eight twelfths, because we multiply the top and the bottom by four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three fourths is nine twelfths, using three.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the top numbers. Eight plus nine is seventeen, so the sum is seventeen twelfths.

beats.colours: the whole = teal, the 5 extra parts = amber
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step four, twelve twelfths make one whole, so seventeen twelfths is one whole and five twelfths.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2/3 > 1/2 and 3/4 > 1/2, so the sum is more than 1 litre

marks.half: both tins are marked above the half litre line
marks.more: the words more than 1 litre are written

narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Each paint is more than half a litre, so together they are more than one litre.

marks.ans: 17/12 litres = 1 5/12 litres is written and glows

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_7}} makes seventeen twelfths of a litre, which is one and five twelfths litres of green paint.
